mcqs.question: [Direct Recall] What monetary policy stance did the RBI adopt on 7 October 2026?
mcqs.explanation: The RBI changed its stance from “Neutral” to “Calibrated Tightening.” “Neutral” was the previous stance, not the new one.

mcqs.question: [Negative / Incorrect Statement] Which of the following statements regarding the RBI’s 7 October 2026 rate decision is incorrect?
options: The repo rate was set at 5.50%.
The SDF rate was set at 5.25%.
The repo rate was set at 5.75%.
The MSF and Bank Rate were set at 5.75%.
mcqs.explanation: The incorrect statement is that the repo rate was set at 5.75%; its correct level was 5.50%. The 5.75% figure applied to the MSF and Bank Rate.

mcqs.question:
[Assertion-Reason] Assertion (A): The RBI’s Monetary Policy Committee decision on 7 October 2026 was unanimous.
Reason (R): The MPC has 6 members, comprising 3 RBI members and 3 Centre members.
options: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true, but R is NOT the correct explanation of A
A is true, but R is false
A is false, but R is true
mcqs.explanation: Both statements are true: the decision was unanimous, and the MPC has 6 members divided equally between the RBI and the Centre. However, the composition of the MPC does not explain why that particular decision was unanimous.

mcqs.question:
[Multi-Statement Correctness] With reference to GST collections in September 2026, consider the following statements:
1. Domestic GST collection was ₹1,37,996 crore.
2. GST collection from imports was ₹65,525 crore.
3. Net GST collection was ₹2,03,521 crore.
mcqs.explanation: Statements 1 and 2 are correct: domestic GST was ₹1,37,996 crore and imports contributed ₹65,525 crore. Statement 3 is incorrect because ₹2,03,521 crore was gross GST, while net GST was ₹1,76,520 crore.

mcqs.question:
[List-Matching] Match the State with its September 2026 GST growth rate.

List-I
(a) Telangana
(b) Karnataka
(c) Kerala
(d) Andhra Pradesh

List-II
i. 6%
ii. 18%
iii. 11%
iv. 16%
mcqs.explanation: The correct pairs are Telangana–18%, Karnataka–16%, Kerala–11%, and Andhra Pradesh–6%, represented by a-ii, b-iv, c-iii, d-i. The other codes interchange the reported growth rates among these States.

mcqs.question: [Direct Recall] Which Article of the Constitution provides for the GST Council?
mcqs.explanation: The GST Council is provided for under Article 279A. The 101st Amendment Act 2016 is an Act, not an Article, and 2017 is associated with the CGST Act.

mcqs.question: [Negative / Incorrect Statement] Which of the following statements about the 57th GST Council’s recommendations is incorrect?
options: The prosecution threshold was recommended to be raised from ₹1 crore to ₹5 crore.
Arrest provisions under GST were recommended for removal.
Interception of goods in transit was recommended to be intelligence-based with authorised approval.
The prosecution threshold was recommended to be reduced from ₹5 crore to ₹1 crore.
mcqs.explanation: The incorrect statement reverses the recommended change: the prosecution threshold was to rise from ₹1 crore to ₹5 crore. The Council also recommended removing arrest provisions and making interception intelligence-based with authorised approval.

mcqs.question:
[Assertion-Reason] Assertion (A): A GST Council decision requires three-fourths of the weighted votes of members present and voting.
Reason (R): The Centre has one-third of the weighted votes and the States together have two-thirds.
options: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true, but R is NOT the correct explanation of A
A is true, but R is false
A is false, but R is true
mcqs.explanation: Both statements are true, and the distribution of weighted votes explains the three-fourths requirement. The Centre has one-third and the States have two-thirds of the weighted votes.

mcqs.question:
[Statement-Based (A/B)] Consider the following statements:
Statement A: Real GDP is measured at constant prices.
Statement B: Nominal GDP is measured at current prices.
options: Both Statement A and Statement B are true
Both Statement A and Statement B are false
Statement A is true, Statement B is false
Statement A is false, Statement B is true
mcqs.explanation: Both statements are true. Real GDP uses constant prices, whereas nominal GDP uses current prices; therefore neither statement reverses the definitions.

mcqs.question: [Negative / Incorrect Statement] Which of the following statements about the National Accounts Statistics 2026 is incorrect?
options: It was released by MoSPI on 31 August 2026.
It was released by the IMF on 31 August 2026.
It introduced 2022–23 as the new base year, replacing 2011–12.
mcqs.explanation: The incorrect statement attributes the release to the IMF; it was released by MoSPI. The publication contained 60 statistical statements and introduced 2022–23 as the new base year, replacing 2011–12.

mcqs.question:
[List-Matching] Match the year with the real GDP growth reported in the National Accounts Statistics 2026.

List-I
(a) 2023–24
(b) 2024–25
(c) 2025–26
(d) Q1 2026–27

List-II
i. 7.8%
ii. 7.2%
iii. 7.3%
iv. 7.8%
mcqs.explanation: The correct pairs are 2023–24–7.3%, 2024–25–7.2%, 2025–26–7.8%, and Q1 2026–27–7.8%, represented by a-iii, b-ii, c-i, d-iv. The two 7.8% entries must be distinguished by their respective year or quarter.

mcqs.question:
[Chronological Ordering] Arrange the following developments in chronological order:
1. Introduction of the new GDP base year 2022–23
2. Enactment of the 101st Amendment Act
3. Launch of GST
4. RBI repo-rate decision of 7 October 2026
mcqs.explanation: The correct order is 2-3-1-4: the 101st Amendment Act was in 2016, GST began on 1 July 2017, the new base year was introduced on 27 February 2026, and the RBI decision occurred on 7 October 2026. The alternatives place at least one later development before an earlier one.

mcqs.question: [Direct Recall] According to the IMF World Economic Outlook of October 2026, what was India’s projected real growth for FY 2026–27?
mcqs.explanation: The IMF projected India’s FY 2026–27 growth at 7.0%, revised up from 6.4%. The 7.4% figure refers to India’s calendar-year growth projection for 2026, not FY 2026–27.

mcqs.question:
[Count-Based] With reference to the IMF and its October 2026 World Economic Outlook, how many of the following statements are correct?
1. The IMF headquarters is in Washington DC.
2. The WEO is published in April and October.
3. SDRs were introduced in 1969.
4. Domestic demand and services were identified as drivers of India’s growth.
mcqs.explanation: All four statements are correct: the IMF is headquartered in Washington DC, the WEO appears in April and October, SDRs were introduced in 1969, and domestic demand and services were identified as growth drivers. Therefore, “All four” is correct.

mcqs.question: Which combination correctly identifies the headquarters and President of the World Bank?
mcqs.explanation: The World Bank is headquartered in Washington DC and its President is Ajay Banga. Mumbai and Sanjay Malhotra are associated with the RBI, not the World Bank.

mcqs.question: GDP estimates in the cited economic data are prepared by which organisation, using which base year?
mcqs.explanation: GDP estimates are prepared by the NSO, with 2022–23 as the base year. The Office of the Economic Adviser prepares WPI data, while CPI is issued by the NSO under MoSPI.

mcqs.question: Net FDI in July 2026 reached what amount, according to the RBI Monthly Bulletin of September 2026?
mcqs.explanation: Net FDI in July 2026 was USD 7.35 billion, the highest since USD 8.80 billion in May 2021. USD 8.80 billion was the earlier high, not the July 2026 figure.

mcqs.question: Which of the following statements regarding India’s price indices is incorrect?
options: CPI is prepared by the NSO under MoSPI.
WPI is prepared by the Office of the Economic Adviser, DPIIT.
The MPC was introduced through an amendment to the RBI Act in 2016.
WPI is prepared by the NSO under MoSPI.
mcqs.explanation: The incorrect statement is that WPI is prepared by the NSO under MoSPI. WPI is prepared by the Office of the Economic Adviser, DPIIT; CPI is prepared by the NSO under MoSPI.

mcqs.question: Which statement about the implementation of Green Energy Corridor Phase-III is incorrect?
options: Greenfield projects use Tariff-Based Competitive Bidding.
Brownfield projects use Tariff-Based Competitive Bidding through Transmission Service Providers.
Brownfield projects are implemented on a Cost Plus Basis.
Greenfield projects follow the BOOM model through Transmission Service Providers.
mcqs.explanation: The incorrect statement is that brownfield projects use Tariff-Based Competitive Bidding through Transmission Service Providers. Greenfield projects use TBCB and the BOOM model, whereas brownfield projects follow the Cost Plus Basis.

mcqs.question:
With reference to state-wise CPI inflation in September 2026, consider the following statements:
1. Uttar Pradesh recorded the highest inflation among the cited States.
2. Andhra Pradesh recorded a higher rate than Telangana.
3. Telangana slipped to fourth place after being highest during January–August 2026.
mcqs.explanation: Statements 1 and 3 are correct: Uttar Pradesh was highest at 6.81%, and Telangana slipped to fourth after being highest during January–August 2026. Statement 2 is incorrect because Telangana’s 6.64% was higher than Andhra Pradesh’s 6.29%.

mcqs.question:
Consider the following statements about foreign direct investment in India:
1. Net FDI equals gross inward FDI minus outward FDI and repatriation/disinvestment.
2. DPIIT is responsible for FDI policy.
3. FDI can come through Automatic and Government routes.
mcqs.explanation: All three statements are correct. Net FDI is calculated after subtracting outward FDI and repatriation/disinvestment from gross inward FDI, while DPIIT handles FDI policy through Automatic and Government routes.

mcqs.question:
Match the components of the PM-DHARA scheme with their cited amounts.

List-I
(a) Total outlay
(b) Intra-State transmission
(c) 50 GWh BESS
(d) Central Financial Support

List-II
(i) ₹50,000 crore
(ii) ₹1,86,405 crore
(iii) ₹54,082 crore
(iv) ₹1,36,378 crore
mcqs.explanation: The correct pairs are a-ii, b-iv, c-i and d-iii. Thus, the total outlay is ₹1,86,405 crore, intra-State transmission is ₹1,36,378 crore, the 50 GWh BESS component is ₹50,000 crore, and Central Financial Support is ₹54,082 crore.

mcqs.question:
Match the Green Energy Corridor Phase-III feature with its corresponding description.

List-I
(a) Greenfield projects
(b) Brownfield projects
(c) Overall implementing agencies
(d) Intra-State transmission component

List-II
(i) State Transmission Utilities
(ii) GEC-III
(iii) Cost Plus Basis
(iv) TBCB and BOOM model through Transmission Service Providers
mcqs.explanation: The correct matching is a-iv, b-iii, c-i and d-ii. Greenfield projects use TBCB and the BOOM model, brownfield projects use the Cost Plus Basis, State Transmission Utilities implement the scheme, and the Intra-State transmission component is GEC-III.

mcqs.question:
Assertion (A): PM-DHARA marks the first time that Green Energy Corridor has included a dedicated battery-storage component.
Reason (R): The scheme contains a 50 GWh BESS component.
options: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true, but R is NOT the correct explanation of A
A is true, but R is false
A is false, but R is true
mcqs.explanation: Both the assertion and the reason are true, and the reason explains the assertion. PM-DHARA includes a 50 GWh BESS component, and this is identified as the first dedicated battery-storage component in the Green Energy Corridor.

mcqs.question:
Consider the following statements:
Statement A: Net FDI is calculated by subtracting outward FDI and repatriation/disinvestment from gross inward FDI.
Statement B: FDI policy is handled by DPIIT through Automatic and Government routes.
options: Both Statement A and Statement B are true
Both Statement A and Statement B are false
Statement A is true, Statement B is false
Statement A is false, Statement B is true
mcqs.explanation: Both statements are true. Net FDI uses the stated subtraction formula, and DPIIT handles FDI policy through the Automatic and Government routes.

mcqs.question:
How many of the following are identified as energy-storage types in the Green Energy Corridor context?
1. Pumped hydro
2. BESS using lithium iron phosphate
3. CSP molten salt
4. Compressed air
mcqs.explanation: All four listed items are identified as storage types: pumped hydro, BESS using lithium iron phosphate, CSP molten salt and compressed air. Therefore, the correct answer is All four.

mcqs.question: Which statement correctly describes the Cabinet-approved PM-DHARA scheme?
options: It was approved in April 2026 and enables evacuation of up to 900 GW by FY 2030–31.
It was approved on 30 September 2026 and enables evacuation of up to 135 GW of renewable energy by FY 2032–33.
It was approved on 30 September 2026 and enables evacuation of up to 50 GWh by FY 2032–33.
It was approved in July 2026 and enables evacuation of up to 135 GW by FY 2025–26.
mcqs.explanation: PM-DHARA was approved by the Union Cabinet on 30 September 2026 and provides for evacuation of up to 135 GW of renewable energy, with completion by FY 2032–33. The other options mix the scheme’s capacity, storage figure, targets or unrelated dates.

mcqs.question: [Direct Recall] What is the Bharat Maritime Insurance Pool (BMIP) primarily designed to provide?
options: India’s first collective domestic platform for insuring large maritime risks
An Alternative Investment Fund for scalable manufacturing enterprises
A reinsurance arrangement for micro enterprises
A fund for financing inland waterways
mcqs.explanation: BMIP is India’s first collective domestic platform for insuring large maritime risks. The Alternative Investment Fund is the form of the SME Growth Fund, not BMIP.

mcqs.question: [Direct Recall] Which institution administers the Bharat Maritime Insurance Pool?
options: General Insurance Corporation of India (GIC Re)
mcqs.explanation: GIC Re administers BMIP. New India Assurance issued the first policy and the first P&I policy, while the International Group of P&I Clubs consists of 13 clubs.

mcqs.question: [Direct Recall] What are the capacity and sovereign-guarantee amounts of BMIP?
mcqs.explanation: BMIP has a capacity of ₹13,906.50 crore and a sovereign guarantee of ₹12,980 crore. ₹10,000 crore is the Government commitment to the SME Growth Fund, while ₹2,000 crore was given additionally to the Self-Reliant India Fund for micro enterprises.

mcqs.question: [Direct Recall] In what form was the ₹10,000-crore SME Growth Fund established?
options: A sovereign guarantee pool for maritime war risks
An Alternative Investment Fund making direct equity investments
A reinsurance reserve for large ships
A grant scheme exclusively for micro enterprises
mcqs.explanation: The SME Growth Fund is an Alternative Investment Fund making direct equity investments as patient growth equity. BMIP is the maritime risk platform with a sovereign guarantee, and the SME Growth Fund is not meant exclusively for micro enterprises.

mcqs.question: [Direct Recall] Which enterprises are targeted by the SME Growth Fund?
options: Viable, scalable small and medium enterprises, mainly manufacturing, including clusters in Tier-II/III cities
Micro enterprises exclusively in metropolitan cities
Large maritime insurers operating from major ports
Enterprises with investment up to ₹2.5 crore and turnover up to ₹10 crore only
mcqs.explanation: The fund targets viable, scalable small and medium enterprises, mainly in manufacturing and clusters in Tier-II/III cities. It is not for micro enterprises; the micro classification allows investment up to ₹2.5 crore and turnover up to ₹10 crore.

mcqs.question: [Negative / Incorrect Statement] With reference to BMIP eligibility, which of the following is incorrect?
options: Vessels owned or managed by Indian entities may be eligible.
Eligibility is confined only to Indian-flagged ships.
Cargo to or from India may be eligible.
The pool covers maritime risks beyond only Indian-flagged ships.
mcqs.explanation: The incorrect statement is that eligibility is confined only to Indian-flagged ships. BMIP also covers vessels owned or managed by Indian entities and cargo to or from India.

mcqs.question: [Negative / Incorrect Statement] Which statement about BMIP claims and the sovereign guarantee is incorrect?
options: Claims up to USD 100 million can come from reserves or reinsurance.
The sovereign guarantee is available before reserves and reinsurance are exhausted.
The sovereign guarantee is used only after reserves are exhausted.
The pool combines reserves or reinsurance with a sovereign guarantee mechanism.
mcqs.explanation: The incorrect statement reverses the claims sequence: the sovereign guarantee is not available before reserves and reinsurance are exhausted. Claims up to USD 100 million are met from reserves or reinsurance first.

mcqs.question:
[Multi-Statement Correctness] Which of the following are covered by BMIP?
1. Hull & Machinery
2. Cargo War
3. Protection & Indemnity (P&I)
mcqs.explanation: BMIP covers Hull & Machinery, Cargo War and Protection & Indemnity (P&I), along with war-perils. Therefore, all three listed statements are correct.

mcqs.question:
[Multi-Statement Correctness] According to the Economic Survey 2025–26, which statements about MSMEs are correct?
1. MSMEs account for 31.1% of GDP.
2. MSMEs account for 35.4% of manufacturing output.
3. MSMEs account for 48.58% of exports.
mcqs.explanation: The Economic Survey 2025–26 figures are 31.1% of GDP, 35.4% of manufacturing output and 48.58% of exports. Hence, all three statements are correct.

mcqs.question:
[List-Matching] Match the MSME category in List-I with its maximum investment and turnover in List-II.

List-I
(a) Small
(b) Medium
(c) Micro
(d) SME Growth Fund

List-II
(i) Investment up to ₹2.5 crore; turnover up to ₹10 crore
(ii) Investment up to ₹25 crore; turnover up to ₹100 crore
(iii) Investment up to ₹125 crore; turnover up to ₹500 crore
(iv) Government commitment of ₹10,000 crore
mcqs.explanation: The correct pairs are a-ii, b-iii, c-i and d-iv. Small enterprises have the ₹25-crore investment and ₹100-crore turnover limits; medium enterprises have ₹125 crore and ₹500 crore, while micro enterprises have ₹2.5 crore and ₹10 crore.

mcqs.question:
[List-Matching] Match the BMIP milestone in List-I with the corresponding detail in List-II.

List-I
(a) First policy
(b) First P&I policy
(c) BMIP administrator
(d) BMIP duration

List-II
(i) General Insurance Corporation of India (GIC Re)
(ii) 30 July 2026
(iii) 10 years, extendable to a maximum of 15 years
(iv) 12 May 2026
mcqs.explanation: The correct pairs are a-iv, b-ii, c-i and d-iii. The first policy was issued on 12 May 2026, the first P&I policy on 30 July 2026, GIC Re is the administrator, and the duration is 10 years extendable to a maximum of 15 years.

mcqs.question:
[Assertion-Reason] Assertion (A): BMIP helped reduce war-risk premiums by 35–40% from the peak during the West Asia conflict.
Reason (R): BMIP was operationalised in May 2026.
options: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true, but R is NOT the correct explanation of A
A is true, but R is false
A is false, but R is true
mcqs.explanation: Both the premium reduction of 35–40% and BMIP’s operationalisation in May 2026 are stated facts. However, operationalisation in May 2026 does not by itself constitute the stated explanation for the premium reduction.

mcqs.question:
[Assertion-Reason] Assertion (A): The SME Growth Fund is not intended for micro enterprises.
Reason (R): The Budget provided ₹2,000 crore additionally to the Self-Reliant India Fund for micro enterprises.
options: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true, but R is NOT the correct explanation of A
A is true, but R is false
A is false, but R is true
mcqs.explanation: Both the exclusion of micro enterprises from the SME Growth Fund and the additional ₹2,000 crore allocation to the Self-Reliant India Fund are correct. The additional allocation is a separate Budget measure and is not the stated reason for the SME Growth Fund’s target design.

mcqs.question:
[Count-Based] How many of the following statements are correct regarding MSMEs as recorded on 6 October 2026?
1. Udyam and Udyam Assist had about 9.78 crore registrations.
2. The number of jobs was 43.28 crore.
3. Women-owned enterprises accounted for 37.6%.
4. Manufacturing registrations numbered 4.08 crore.
mcqs.explanation: The first three statements are correct: registrations were about 9.78 crore, jobs were 43.28 crore and women-owned enterprises accounted for 37.6%. The figure 4.08 crore refers to trading, while manufacturing registrations numbered 1.93 crore.

mcqs.question:
[Chronological Ordering] Arrange the following events in chronological order:
1. Cabinet approval of the SME Growth Fund
2. Approval of BMIP
3. Launch of BMIP
4. First P&I policy under BMIP
mcqs.explanation: The correct order is BMIP approval on 18 April 2026, BMIP launch on 12 May 2026, the first P&I policy on 30 July 2026, and SME Growth Fund Cabinet approval on 6 October 2026. Thus, the sequence is 2-3-4-1.

mcqs.question: What is the planning horizon of the National Transport Master Plan to be prepared by ITLA?
mcqs.explanation: ITLA will prepare the National Transport Master Plan with a horizon of 10 years or more. The five-year option is a trap linked to the five-year completion of PM Gati Shakti, not the Transport Master Plan.

mcqs.question: With reference to ITLA’s appraisal function, identify the incorrect statement.
options: ITLA will technically appraise central projects costing ₹500 crore or more.
ITLA will technically appraise central projects costing ₹250 crore or more.
Financial appraisal will continue through existing mechanisms.
ITLA is an SPV for research, planning, appraisal and monitoring.
mcqs.explanation: The incorrect statement changes the threshold from ₹500 crore to ₹250 crore. ITLA’s technical appraisal applies to central projects of ₹500 crore or more, while financial appraisal remains through existing mechanisms.

mcqs.question:
Consider the following statements about the PM Gati Shakti National Master Plan:
1. It is a GIS-based platform.
2. It connects 58 Central Ministries and all 36 States and Union Territories.
3. DPIIT is its nodal department.
mcqs.explanation: All three statements are correct. PM Gati Shakti is GIS-based, connects 58 Central Ministries and all 36 States and Union Territories, and has DPIIT as its nodal department.

mcqs.question:
Consider the following statements:
Statement A: India is the second-largest steel producer after China.
Statement B: worldsteel was established in 1967 in Brussels and SAIL was established in 1973.
options: Both Statement A and Statement B are true
Both Statement A and Statement B are false
Statement A is true, Statement B is false
Statement A is false, Statement B is true
mcqs.explanation: Both statements are true. India is the second-largest producer after China; worldsteel dates to 1967 in Brussels, while SAIL was established in 1973.

mcqs.question: Identify the incorrect statement regarding the 2026–27 foodgrain targets.
options: The 2026–27 overall target is higher than the 2025–26 record of 376.56 million tonnes.
The Rabi target is 177.72 million tonnes.
The Rabi target is higher than the 2025–26 Rabi range of 171.14–174.51 million tonnes.
The overall foodgrain target is 373.93 million tonnes.
mcqs.explanation: The incorrect statement reverses the comparison: 373.93 million tonnes is slightly lower than the 2025–26 record of 376.56 million tonnes. The Rabi target of 177.72 million tonnes is higher than the 2025–26 range of 171.14–174.51 million tonnes.

mcqs.question:
How many of the above statements are correct?
1. Kharif crops are sown with the southwest monsoon and harvested in autumn.
2. Rice is the principal cereal associated with Kharif.
3. Rabi crops are sown in winter and harvested in spring.
4. Rabi crops are sown with the southwest monsoon and harvested in autumn.
mcqs.explanation: Statements 1, 2 and 3 are correct, so the answer is Only three. Statement 4 describes the Kharif season; Rabi crops are sown in winter and harvested in spring.

mcqs.question: From 2016–17 to 2025–26, by approximately how many times did the value of India’s pulses exports increase?
mcqs.explanation: The value of pulses exports increased from US$191.76 million in 2016–17 to US$969.58 million in 2025–26, or approximately five times. The approximately sevenfold figure refers to the increase in export volume, not export value.

mcqs.question: Which GI-tagged product from Karnataka has been in demand in Maldives at prices up to 30% higher?
mcqs.explanation: Kalaburagi Tur Dal, a GI product from Karnataka, has been in demand in Maldives at prices up to 30% higher. The other options are cereals or do not identify the specified GI pulses product.

mcqs.question:
Assertion (A): The Bankers’ Books Evidence Act–2026 recognises physical, electronic and digital banking records as evidence.
Reason (R): The Act requires standards of accuracy, authenticity, integrity and anti-tampering.
options: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true, but R is NOT the correct explanation of A
A is true, but R is false
A is false, but R is true
mcqs.explanation: Both the Assertion and the Reason are true. However, the listed standards describe the requirements for reliable records and do not themselves explain the Act’s recognition of physical, electronic and digital records as evidence.

mcqs.question:
Match List-I with List-II regarding the first post-Independence international cargo voyage from Bogibeel.

List-I
 a. Flagged-off by
 b. Route
 c. Cargo source
 d. NW-2

List-II
 i. Dhubri–Sadiya, 891 km; agency IWAI
 ii. Sarbananda Sonowal
 iii. Methanol from APCL Namrup
 iv. Brahmaputra and Indo–Bangladesh Protocol Route to Pangaon Port, Dhaka
mcqs.explanation: The correct pairs are a-ii, b-iv, c-iii and d-i. Sarbananda Sonowal flagged off the voyage; it used the Brahmaputra and Indo–Bangladesh Protocol Route, carried methanol from APCL Namrup, and used NW-2, the 891-km Dhubri–Sadiya waterway under IWAI.

mcqs.question: What was the theme of the 3rd Sagarmanthan — The Great Oceans Dialogue 2026?
options: Trade, Technology, and Trust at Sea
Resilience in an Age of Flux
Blue Geographies, New Aspirations: Trade, Technology, and Trust at Sea
mcqs.explanation: The theme was “Blue Geographies, New Aspirations: Trade, Technology, and Trust at Sea.” “Resilience in an Age of Flux” was the theme of the Kautilya Economic Conclave, while “Life Below Water” is SDG 14.

mcqs.question: Who inaugurated the 5th Kautilya Economic Conclave on 3 October 2026?
mcqs.explanation: Vice President C.P. Radhakrishnan inaugurated the 5th Kautilya Economic Conclave on 3 October 2026 in New Delhi. The Ministry of Finance and the Institute of Economic Growth were associated with organising the conclave, while Narendra Modi is mentioned in connection with the proposed airport name.

mcqs.question: With reference to NABKISAN Finance Ltd’s WASH Social Bond, which of the following statements is incorrect?
options: It is India’s first WASH Social Bond listed on NSE.
NABKISAN Finance Ltd is a subsidiary of NABARD.
Its proceeds can be used only for eligible green shipping projects.
Its proceeds can be used only for eligible WASH projects.
mcqs.explanation: The incorrect statement is that the proceeds can be used only for eligible green shipping projects. The Use-of-Proceeds model restricts the funds to eligible Water, Sanitation and Hygiene projects.

mcqs.question:
Consider the following statements about the proposed Narendra Modi International Airport, Noida–Jewar:
1. The proposed name was approved by the Uttar Pradesh Cabinet on 9 October 2026.
2. The airport is located in Gautam Buddha Nagar.
3. Commercial flights began from 15 June 2026.
mcqs.explanation: All three statements are correct: the Uttar Pradesh Cabinet approved the proposed renaming on 9 October 2026, the airport is in Gautam Buddha Nagar, and commercial flights began from 15 June 2026. The final decision still requires Union Cabinet approval and a Gazette notification.

mcqs.question:
Match List-I with List-II:

List-I
 a. Sagarmanthan — The Great Oceans Dialogue
 b. Kautilya Economic Conclave
 c. WASH Social Bond
 d. International Maritime Organization

List-II
 i. NABKISAN Finance Ltd
 ii. Ministry of Ports, Shipping and Waterways with ORF
 iii. Established in 1948 with headquarters in London
 iv. Institute of Economic Growth with Ministry of Finance
mcqs.explanation: The correct pairs are a-ii, b-iv, c-i and d-iii. Sagarmanthan is organised by the Ministry of Ports, Shipping and Waterways with ORF; the Kautilya conclave is organised by IEG with the Ministry of Finance; NABKISAN issued the bond; and IMO was established in 1948 with headquarters in London.

mcqs.question:
Assertion (A): The India–EU Green Shipping Corridor industry coalition was launched to export Indian green ammonia and green methanol to Europe.
Reason (R): The initiative was based on a 2025 pre-feasibility study.
options: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true, but R is NOT the correct explanation of A
A is true, but R is false
A is false, but R is true
mcqs.explanation: Both the Assertion and the Reason are true. The coalition was launched for exporting Indian green ammonia and green methanol to Europe, and it was based on a 2025 pre-feasibility study; however, the study’s existence does not itself explain the stated export purpose.

mcqs.question:
Consider the following statements:
Statement A: The Uttar Pradesh Cabinet decided to rename the Noida–Jewar airport as Narendra Modi International Airport, Noida–Jewar.
Statement B: The final decision requires Union Cabinet approval and a Gazette notification.
options: Both Statement A and Statement B are true
Both Statement A and Statement B are false
Statement A is true, Statement B is false
Statement A is false, Statement B is true
mcqs.explanation: Both statements are true. The Uttar Pradesh Cabinet made the renaming decision on 9 October 2026, but the final decision requires approval by the Union Cabinet followed by a Gazette notification.

mcqs.question:
How many of the following institutions or entities were established before 1950?
1. Observer Research Foundation
2. International Maritime Organization
3. European Union
4. Airports Authority of India
mcqs.explanation: Only one entity was established before 1950: the International Maritime Organization, established in 1948. ORF was established in 1990, the European Union is associated with the Maastricht Treaty of 1993, and AAI was established in 1995.

mcqs.question: The Reserve Bank of India’s repo-rate decision of 7 October 2026 marked the first hike since which month and year?
mcqs.explanation: The 7 October 2026 decision was the first repo-rate hike since February 2023. February 2025 is incorrect because the fact specifies that the hike followed cuts in 2025.

mcqs.question: Which of the following statements regarding India’s inflation target is incorrect?
options: The CPI inflation target is 4% with a tolerance of 2% on either side.
The CPI inflation target is 4% with a tolerance of 3% on either side.
The target framework is expressed around 4% CPI inflation with a 2% tolerance band.
The target is set by the Centre in consultation with the RBI.
mcqs.explanation: The incorrect statement changes the tolerance band from 2% to 3%. India’s CPI inflation target is 4% with a tolerance of 2% on either side, set by the Centre in consultation with the RBI.

mcqs.question: Which recommendation of the 57th GST Council meeting specifically concerned small e-commerce sellers?
options: Simpler registration for small manufacturing units
Simpler registration for large e-commerce platforms
Simpler registration for small e-commerce sellers
mcqs.explanation: The recommendation was to provide simpler registration for small e-commerce sellers. The alternatives change the category of businesses covered and therefore do not match the recommendation.

mcqs.question:
With reference to the National Accounts Statistics 2026, consider the following statements:
Statement A: Final estimates were provided for 2022–23 and 2023–24.
Statement B: The estimate for 2024–25 was the first revised estimate.
options: Both Statement A and Statement B are true
Both Statement A and Statement B are false
Statement A is true, Statement B is false
Statement A is false, Statement B is true
mcqs.explanation: Both statements are true: the estimates for 2022–23 and 2023–24 were final estimates, while 2024–25 received its first revised estimate. Hence, the options treating either statement as false are incorrect.

mcqs.question:
With reference to the World Bank’s assessment of India’s economic growth, consider the following statements:
Statement A: India’s FY 2026–27 growth forecast was 7.1%.
Statement B: India recorded 7.8% growth in the first quarter.
options: Both Statement A and Statement B are true
Both Statement A and Statement B are false
Statement A is true, Statement B is false
Statement A is false, Statement B is true
mcqs.explanation: Both statements are true: the World Bank forecast India’s FY 2026–27 growth at 7.1%, while first-quarter growth was 7.8%. The other options incorrectly treat one or both of these figures as incorrect.

mcqs.question: With reference to India’s CPI inflation in September 2026, which of the following statements is incorrect?
options: CPI inflation remained within the 2–5% tolerance band.
CPI inflation was above the 4% target.
CPI inflation remained within the 2–6% tolerance band.
CPI inflation was 5.54%, the highest since 6.25% in October 2024.
mcqs.explanation: The incorrect statement is that inflation remained within the 2–5% band. The cited tolerance band was 2–6%; September 2026 CPI inflation was 5.54%, above the 4% target but within that band.

mcqs.question:
With reference to renewable-energy transmission and power curtailment, consider the following statements:
1. Approximately 6,900 GWh of clean power was restricted in FY 2025–26.
2. Peak demand reached a record 270 GW during April–June 2026.
3. Approximately 8,133 GWh of solar power was curtailed during April–June 2026.
mcqs.explanation: All three statements are correct. Clean-power restriction was approximately 6,900 GWh in FY 2025–26, while April–June 2026 saw record peak demand of 270 GW and solar curtailment of approximately 8,133 GWh.

mcqs.question: Green Energy Corridor Phase-II was implemented across how many States?
mcqs.explanation: Green Energy Corridor Phase-II covered 7 States. The same phase involved 7,863 ckm of lines and 24,388 MVA of capacity; the other choices do not match its stated coverage.

mcqs.question:
With reference to India’s energy-transition targets, how many of the following statements are correct?
1. Renewable-energy capacity is targeted to increase from 295 GW to 500 GW by 2030.
2. Non-fossil capacity is targeted to reach 900 GW by 2035.
3. Renewable-energy capacity is targeted to reach 500 GW by 2035.
4. Non-fossil capacity is targeted to reach 900 GW by 2030.
mcqs.explanation: Only statements 1 and 2 are correct: the targets are 500 GW of renewable energy by 2030 and 900 GW of non-fossil capacity by 2035. Statements 3 and 4 interchange the specified target years.

mcqs.question: Under the BMIP achievements recorded by 7 September 2026, which pair was listed among the other beneficiaries apart from the first policies?
options: Hoger Offshore and Marine Pvt Ltd and Shipping Corporation of India
Vedanta Sterlite Copper and Balrampur Chini Mills
New India Assurance and General Insurance Corporation of India
mcqs.explanation: Vedanta Sterlite Copper and Balrampur Chini Mills were listed among the other BMIP beneficiaries. Hoger Offshore and Marine Pvt Ltd and Shipping Corporation of India were associated with the first policies, not this pair.

mcqs.question: With reference to BMIP achievements recorded by 7 September 2026, which of the following statements is incorrect?
options: 92 Hull War-risk policies had been issued.
3,000 Cargo War policies had been issued.
mcqs.explanation: The incorrect statement is that 2 P&I policies had been issued; the correct number was 3. The other figures—3,000 Cargo War policies and 92 Hull War-risk policies—are correct.

mcqs.question:
Which of the following schemes were listed among the other MSME schemes?

1. CGTMSE
2. PM Vishwakarma
3. National SC-ST Hub
mcqs.explanation: CGTMSE, PM Vishwakarma and the National SC-ST Hub were all listed among the other MSME schemes. Therefore, statements 1, 2 and 3 are correct.

mcqs.question:
Match the maritime-sector indicator in List-I with the corresponding figure in List-II.

List-I
(a) Maritime trade by value
(b) Maritime trade by volume
(c) Ports
(d) Fleet in mid-2026

List-II
(i) 1,609 ships and 14.33 million GT
(ii) 12 major and 217 non-major
(iii) About 95%
(iv) About 70%
mcqs.explanation: The correct pairs are a-iii, b-iv, c-ii and d-i: maritime trade accounts for about 95% by value and 70% by volume, there are 12 major and 217 non-major ports, and the mid-2026 fleet had 1,609 ships and 14.33 million GT. The other codes interchange these sectoral indicators.

mcqs.question:
Assertion (A): India's maritime trade accounts for about 95% by value and 70% by volume.
Reason (R): India's annual P&I premium outflow is about USD 45–60 million.
options: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true, but R is NOT the correct explanation of A
A is true, but R is false
A is false, but R is true
mcqs.explanation: Both the assertion and the reason are true: maritime trade accounts for about 95% by value and 70% by volume, while annual P&I premium outflow is about USD 45–60 million. However, the premium outflow does not explain the composition of maritime trade by value and volume.

mcqs.question:
Consider the following statements:

Statement A: The SME Growth Fund's Alternative Investment Fund is regulated by SEBI under the SEBI (AIF) Regulations, 2012.
Statement B: The AIF has only Category I and Category II classifications.
options: Both Statement A and Statement B are true
Both Statement A and Statement B are false
Statement A is true, Statement B is false
Statement A is false, Statement B is true
mcqs.explanation: Statement A is true because the AIF is regulated by SEBI under the SEBI (AIF) Regulations, 2012. Statement B is false because the classifications include Category I, Category II and Category III.

mcqs.question:
[Multi-Statement Correctness] With reference to the targets in the Draft National Steel Policy 2047, consider the following statements:
1. Crude steel capacity is targeted at 604 MT by 2047.
2. Finished steel demand is targeted at 505 MT.
3. Steel exports are targeted at 45 MT.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
mcqs.explanation: All three statements are correct: the targets are 604 MT for crude steel capacity, 505 MT for finished steel demand and 45 MT for exports. The alternatives excluding one statement incorrectly omit one of these Draft National Steel Policy 2047 targets.

mcqs.question: [Negative / Incorrect Statement] Which one of the following statements regarding the Draft National Steel Policy 2047 is incorrect?
options: The policy proposes support to the secondary steel sector.
The secondary steel sector covers approximately 2,550 units and 45% of capacity.
The units include those using electric arc furnaces and induction furnaces.
The secondary steel sector accounts for approximately 47% of capacity.
mcqs.explanation: The incorrect statement changes the capacity share from approximately 47% to 45%. The Draft National Steel Policy 2047 refers to approximately 2,550 secondary steel units accounting for 47% of capacity, including electric arc and induction furnaces.

mcqs.question: [Direct Recall] Who announced India’s foodgrain target of 373.93 million tonnes for 2026–27?
mcqs.explanation: The 2026–27 foodgrain target was announced by Agriculture Minister Shivraj Singh Chouhan on 29 September 2026. PM Modi, Sarbananda Sonowal and the Department of Commerce through DGFT are associated with other developments, not this announcement.

mcqs.question:
[Assertion-Reason] Assertion (A): India remains a net importer of pulses.
Reason (R): India imports approximately 60 lakh tonnes of pulses annually.
options: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true, but R is NOT the correct explanation of A
A is true, but R is false
A is false, but R is true
mcqs.explanation: Both the assertion and the reason are true, and annual imports of approximately 60 lakh tonnes explain why India remains a net importer. India is also first in production, consumption and import of pulses, but that does not alter its net-importer status.

mcqs.question: [Direct Recall] The Mission for Aatmanirbharta in Pulses was launched in which year?
mcqs.explanation: The Mission for Aatmanirbharta in Pulses was launched in 2025. The other years are associated with the effective date of RoDTEP, the National Logistics Policy and the extension period of RoDTEP.

mcqs.question:
[List-Matching] Match List-I with List-II regarding the RoDTEP scheme.

List-I
 a. RoDTEP
 b. Effective from and scheme replaced
 c. Notified by
 d. Implemented by

List-II
 i. Remission of Duties and Taxes on Exported Products
 ii. 1 January 2021; replaced MEIS
 iii. Department of Commerce through DGFT
 iv. Department of Revenue through CBIC

Select the correct code:
mcqs.explanation: The correct pairs are a-i, b-ii, c-iii and d-iv. RoDTEP expands to Remission of Duties and Taxes on Exported Products, became effective on 1 January 2021 after replacing MEIS, was notified through DGFT and was implemented through CBIC.

mcqs.question:
[Statement-Based (A/B)] Consider the following statements:
Statement A: The Bankers’ Books Evidence Act–2026 came into force on 1 October 2026.
Statement B: It replaced the Bankers’ Books Evidence Act, 1891.
options: Both Statement A and Statement B are true
Both Statement A and Statement B are false
Statement A is true, Statement B is false
Statement A is false, Statement B is true
mcqs.explanation: Both statements are true. The Bankers’ Books Evidence Act–2026 came into force on 1 October 2026 and replaced the Bankers’ Books Evidence Act, 1891.

mcqs.question: The 3rd Sagarmanthan — The Great Oceans Dialogue 2026 was held at which venue and during which period?
mcqs.explanation: The 3rd Sagarmanthan — The Great Oceans Dialogue 2026 was held in New Delhi from 7–9 October 2026. The tempting alternatives incorrectly shorten the event to a single day or omit the year.
